specs.hypothesis: RE-RUN. In wave 3 this died with 'arena exhausted': building the [M, K*V] logit tensor by chaining op_concat is O(K^2) in memory and at K=8 the intermediates came to 303MB. Fixed by allocating the wide tensor once and placing each head into its column range (op_place). The hypothesis is unchanged: K=8 should be near the point where blind emission destroys coherence, since 7 of every 8 bytes are written without feedback. Included to locate the knee, not because it is expected to be good. Wave 7's adaptive-K8 rescores depend on this checkpoint.

ANSWER TO THE REFLECTION IN SECTION R1. Every variant so far assumes all bytes deserve the same computation. Here a tiny bigram-memory net (its own 32-dim embedding, a 4096-row hashed bigram table, its own unembedding -- ~33KB read per byte, 30x cheaper than the transformer) proposes every byte, and the transformer runs only when the small net's own max probability falls below tau. The two nets share no parameters, so their byte costs are disjoint and countable separately. The transformer still sees every byte, catching up on the backlog in one batched pass whose weights are counted once -- so bytes/token = fast_bytes + big_bytes/(mean run length). Byte-level text should be highly bigram-predictable inside words, so a large fraction of bytes may never need the transformer at all.
